page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. The system is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance but highlights limitations under multi-core workloads. The single-core stress-ng CPU and Geekbench tests register in the average tier, as do single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core benchmarks, including multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core tests, fall into the weak or poor categories. Memory bandwidth tests also show weak performance for both small and large block reads and writes.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource ratio, the instance represents a standard entry-level tier for general-purpose workloads. It is suitable for basic web serving, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded applications. However, the weak multi-core scaling, low memory bandwidth, and lack of local storage make it less suitable for intensive database operations, software compilation, or heavy multi-threaded processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor at 2.7 GHz. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks show average single-core capabilities, particularly in text processing and single-threaded compression. However, multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth are relatively weak, as evidenced by lower scores in multi-threaded decompression and database operations. This hardware profile is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic application hosting, and single-threaded tasks where balanced CPU-to-memory ratios are required without intensive parallel processing demands.
